name: ST14
summary: ST14 encodes matriptase, an enzyme of the skin needed for a sound outer layer and for hair follicles to form. A nonsense change, c.388G>T (p.Glu130*), cuts off more than four fifths of the protein and causes naked foal syndrome in the Akhal-Teke: a foal with almost no hair and dry, scaly skin, most of which have died between a few weeks and three years old. It is recessive, and carriers are normal. In the study that found it, all five affected horses had two copies, 26 of 191 other Akhal-Tekes were carriers, and none of 400 horses of other breeds had it. Why affected foals die early is unresolved; a heart defect and other findings in one foal may be coincidental. The colour of the coat is not affected, only whether hair grows. No effect on build or performance is established.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: ST14 carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy. The horse is normal, with nothing to see, and passes the copy to half its foals. A foal is affected only when both parents pass it on.

phenotypes.name: Naked foal syndrome
phenotypes.description: Two copies. The foal is born with almost no body hair, a sparse or missing mane and tail, short curly whiskers and no eyelashes, over dry, scaly skin. Without hair the skin is easily injured and scarred, and the eyes water. Teeth and hooves were normal in the cases examined. Most known foals died between a few weeks and three years of age, and why is not known; one was alive at nearly three.
